record.paper_title: Known results and open problems in hypercomplex convexity
record.original_question: Suppose D is a bounded domain in H^n with smooth boundary and n > 1, and suppose D is locally linearly convex in the sense that for every boundary point z there exist a left hyperplane l and a neighborhood U(z) such that z lies in l and D ∩ l ∩ U(z) is empty. Must D then be H-convex, meaning that for every hypercomplex line γ the intersection γ ∩ D is acyclic, and must D also be homeomorphic to the 4n-dimensional Euclidean ball R^{4n}?

evidence.quote: Definition 4. A set E ⊂ Hn is called H-convex, if for every hypercomplex line γ intersection γ ∩ E is acyclic.

Definition 5. A domain D in a hypercomplex Euclidean space Hn is called locally linearly convex, if for every point z of the boundary D there exists a left hyperplane l and neighbourhood U(z) then z ∈ l and D ∩ l ∩ U(z) = ∅.

Problem 3. Is this true or not that every bounded locally linearly convex domain in Hn with smooth boundary, n > 1 is H-convex and homeomorphicaly equivalent to 4n-dimensional ball in Euclidean space R4n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of quaternions, and let $\mathbb{H}^n$ be the right $n$-dimensional hypercomplex (quaternionic) Euclidean space, identified as a real vector space with $\mathbb{R}^{4n}$. A left hyperplane in $\mathbb{H}^n$ is an affine subspace of the form $\{z\in\mathbb{H}^n : \sum_{j=1}^n a_j z_j = b\}$ for some fixed $a_1,\dots,a_n,b\in\mathbb{H}$ with not all $a_j$ zero. A hypercomplex line in $\mathbb{H}^n$ is an affine right-quaternionic line, i.e. a set of the form $\{p+t q : t\in\mathbb{H}\}$ for fixed $p,q\in\mathbb{H}^n$, $q\neq 0$.

A set $E\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ is called H-convex if for every hypercomplex line $\gamma$ the intersection $\gamma\cap E$ is acyclic (i.e. has the (Čech, reduced) cohomology of a point whenever it is nonempty).

A domain $D\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ is called locally linearly convex if, for every boundary point $z\in\partial D$, there exist a left hyperplane $\ell$ with $z\in\ell$ and an open neighborhood $U(z)$ of $z$ such that $D\cap\ell\cap U(z)=\emptyset$.

Question. Suppose $n>1$ and $D\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ is a bounded domain with smooth boundary that is locally linearly convex. Must $D$ then be H-convex, and must $D$ be homeomorphic to the closed (or open) 4n-dimensional Euclidean ball in $\mathbb{R}^{4n}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on hypercomplex convexity (it is the local-to-global convexity question for bounded smoothly bounded locally linearly convex domains in H^n, n>1). Web searches turn up only references that restate the problem as open; no resolution (positive or negative) was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3 asks whether every bounded locally linearly convex domain in H^n with smooth boundary, n>1, is H-convex and homeomorphic to the 4n-dimensional ball in R^{4n}.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem in surveys of hypercomplex convexity.

status_evidence.title: Hypercomplex convexity: known results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems in hypercomplex convexity, including the local-to-global convexity question for smoothly bounded locally linearly convex domains.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the problem is reported; it remains stated as open.
